rawContent: ‘Because the boys watching today will be the men of tomorrow’; and the girls watching today will be the women of tomorrow. Thank you Gilette for taking a stand #MeToo #TimesUp

I’m saddened by the fact that anyone asks this question and the fact that journalists do so - and use it to sell a story - really underscores to me how hard it’s going to continue to me for survivors to feel safe in coming forward #metoo
Strong and important words from Emma Thompson #metoo

Grateful to return to @Poynter to deliver workshop with @griviera @thepressforward for #poynterwomenleaders on standing up to sexual harassment; my first time back since Poynter published my experiences of sexual assault as a journalist #metoo

It took me more than a decade to share my experiences of sexual assault as a journalist and sometimes I still find it hard to talk about but I chose to do so to show others they are not alone and that together we can change things #metoo https://t.co/kpruRtl7gA
Here's a link to the piece I wrote for @Poynter about my #metoo experiences. Please take care of yourself if you choose to read it. https://t.co/QLtRVeo0ar
Here’s a piece I wrote about the media’s #metoo problem that we shared for #InternationalWomensDay in the hope that we can start trying to change the culture that facilitates this still

I wrote this about navigating my #metoo story, and the impact it’s had on my life before and after I spoke out. It was hard to write but I’m glad I did and am grateful to @Poynter and @Mel_Grau for their support. I hope it shows others they’re not alone https://t.co/ubGpK8ha6Z
So, I wrote a poem for #WorldPoetryDay. It’s for anyone who’s ever felt the weight of shame and silence. It’s called ‘It’s History, Not His Story’ #amwriting #poetry #metoo https://t.co/gMUlbPYCBC

It’s #WorldPoetryDay so I wrote a poem. It’s called ‘It’s History, Not His Story’ and it’s for anyone who has ever felt the weight of shame and kept silent. Finding the words has been so helpful for me #amwriting #poetry #metoo #MentalHealthAwareness https://t.co/SuAMhv0fTY

Here’s me reading my #WorldPoetryDay poem ‘It’s History, Not His Story’. In speaking about the abuse I experienced I finally broke my silence and so I wrote this #metoo #poetry to be read out loud, even if I am still a #workinprogress much like my #WritingCommunity https://t.co/uhvz8NuK7m

@kenyonreview It took me until the grand old age of 41 and 3/4 to realise I could be authentic and today of all days I found my poetry voice, writing my #metoo poem, 'It's History, Not His Story' and recording it. This speaking out loud poetry was inspired by the brilliant @holliepoetry

I’ve been holding off buying this for a while until the time felt right and after recent days, where I’ve also been able to use my #metoo voice, I’m so excited to finally be reading Vox by @CVDalcher https://t.co/u8CHHhVIhX

So so humbling and hard to hear the brave voices of women sharing their #metoo stories and those from their countries at #ifj19 - thank you @icfjoyce for moderating this extraordinary panel https://t.co/jgdwVeppaG

‘It is very draining emotionally’, says Mijal Iastrebner #ifj19 - we are ‘reliving the trauma’. Our news industry needs to better recognise this and the impact it has on survivors of #metoo professionally and personally.
Digital space is a privilege say @MercyJuma_ - the majority of women in Africa are being left behind. How do we get this movement to them, she asks #metoo #ifj19

In Latin America there is a lot of difficult in trusting and telling the story and getting the words right in #metoo coverage says Mijal Iastrebner #ifj19 - there is a lot of fraternity and powerful men but it is changing

I’ve been so privileged to work with @Poynter and @ThePressForward to develop newsroom training to counter sexual harassment and change culture in the States and would love to speak with anyone who’s interested in knowing more about this #ifj19 #metoo

We need to show the abnormal is abnormal. ‘Stop normalising the atrocities that are being committed to young women and men’ says @mercyjuma. It starts with us (media) and continues with us #metoo #ifj19
Four on quite a few. #metoo conversation with @icfjoyce today, I’m on two, and I know @courtneyr is moderating one tomorrow. We are half of the population: this shouldn’t be surprising

I’m so grateful to be back in Perugia at #ijf19 to take part in today’s panel on ‘Telling gender stories innovatively in the #metoo era’ with these amazing women @julieposetti @IngaThordar @AnnetteF24 @zziomecka

Our #metoo panel was packed @journalismfest and far away from the core of #IJF19. I’m sure it wasn’t conscious but gave a sense of this being away from the mainstream. If we want really want to put gender on the agenda, pls can you consider a bigger more central room next year https://t.co/Nar710gpq5
